matched: Starting valuations, interest rates and profits constrained aggregate returns far below popular expectations → With the 10-year Treasury yielding over 6% and the aggregate market offering an earnings yield of less than 3.5%, the 'new era' enthusiasm has pushed valuations to a point where the margin of safety—our most critical tool—is effectively non-existent
missed: Technological transformation did not automatically produce attractive shareholder economics.
High prices and uncertainty about winners supported withholding new equity capital rather than predicting the next market move.
Existing sound franchises were not automatically sold because the aggregate market was expensive.
extra_agent_drivers: The earnings yield of equities is substantially lower than the risk-free rate provided by long-term government bonds, rendering stocks unattractive by our standard
Broad market valuations, with trailing P/Es near 29x, leave little margin of safety and imply that investors are betting on sustained, rapid earnings growth rather than existing value
Public sentiment displays high return expectations of up to 22.6% annually, contrasting sharply with underlying economic realities and prudent investment logic

spot_checks.claim: The market earnings yield of 3.49% is significantly lower than the 6.09% yield on the 10-year Treasury bond
Equities appear expensive at a trailing P/E of 28.66x

verbatim_agent_sentence: For now, we will hold our wonderful businesses and wait for Mr. Market to offer us prices that reflect business value rather than speculative fervor [D04, D08].
grader_notes: The agent correctly identified the 'HOLD_CASH' stance. Reasoning overlap was limited (k=1); while the agent correctly focused on valuation and interest rate spreads, it failed to incorporate the specific Berkshire-articulated drivers regarding technological transformation and the explicit distinction between holding existing franchises versus withholding new capital.
